intro.author: Traditionally John Mark, a companion of Peter and Paul (Acts 12:12; 1 Peter 5:13). The Gospel itself is anonymous; an early second-century report says Mark wrote down Peter's preaching.
intro.written: Most scholars date it about AD 65–70, often placing it in or near Rome
intro.audience: Mostly Gentile believers, likely in Rome; Mark explains Jewish customs and translates Aramaic words for them
intro.setting: Mark is the shortest Gospel and, in the view of most scholars, the earliest. It moves fast, often linking scenes with 'straightway' (immediately). Many think it was written for Christians facing persecution, possibly in Rome after Nero blamed them for the great fire of AD 64.
intro.purpose: To announce 'the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God' (1:1) and show that the Messiah's path, and his followers' path, runs through suffering to resurrection.
intro.bigIdea: Jesus is the mighty Son of God who came not to be served but to serve and give his life.

outline.title: Authority in Galilee and rising conflict
